name: Thunder from the Steppe: The Mongol World
description: In a single lifetime a clan chief's horsemen built the largest land empire in history; here are its campaigns, cities, rulers and the world it left behind.

checkpoints.name: The rise of Temujin
checkpoints.note: A boy named Temujin, later Genghis Khan, survived feuds on the steppe and gathered tribes under his rule. His general Subutai would become the most able of his commanders.

checkpoints.name: World conquest
checkpoints.note: Proclaimed ruler in 1206, Genghis founded the Mongol Empire. His army crushed the Khwarazmian state and Samarkand, the Golden Horde reached Europe, the Secret History was written, and in 1258 Baghdad was taken.

checkpoints.name: Kublai and the Yuan
checkpoints.note: Kublai Khan became the great khan and ruled China as the Yuan dynasty. The Mamluks stopped the Mongols at Ain Jalut, his fleets failed against Japan, and Marco Polo told Europe of his court.

checkpoints.name: Plague and break-up
checkpoints.note: The khanates drifted apart. Paper money spread, Ibn Battuta travelled under Mongol-ruled lands, and the Black Death moved along the trade routes the Mongols had made safe.

checkpoints.name: The heirs
checkpoints.note: Chinese rebels drove out the Yuan and set up the Ming dynasty. Timur created a new empire from Samarkand, and his descendant Babur founded the Mughal Empire in India.
